name: File tools stay in the working directory unless a folder is added with /add-dir
description: GitHub issue #38: the agent could read, list and search any folder on the machine. The write-only project-root guard (tools::guard) now sits in front of every file tool, reads included (read_file, list_dir, glob, grep; write_file, edit_file, multi_edit, delete_file, move_file as before). A path is judged after canonicalising its deepest existing ancestor, so `..`, symlinks and drive/UNC prefixes resolve first; a dangling symlink fails closed (writing through one would create its target outside); the std-fallback walk and substring grep do not follow a symlink that leaves the allowed folders; rg gets `--` before the path so a path named like a flag stays a path. /add-dir <path> (also --add-dir at launch, repeatable) grants a folder and its subtree for the run, /add-dir alone lists, /add-dir --remove <path> takes one back. A refusal names the allowed folders and tells the model to ask the user for /add-dir. rusti's own docs (~/.rusti/docs) and skill folders stay readable without a grant (the system prompt sends the model there), never writable. Auto mode still only runs unasked what is inside the project root itself (tools::in_root), not an added folder. Devil mode / --yolo lifts the guard as before. NOT covered, stated in docs/safety.md: run_command, run_background, !cmd (the shell reaches any path) and MCP tools.
evidence: Tests written first against the issue's cases, all in ai_core::tools::tests and tui::app::tests: paths_outside_the_working_directory_are_refused (.., src/../.., absolute, not-yet-existing outside paths, every file tool's refusal text), add_dir_grants_its_subtree_and_remove_dir_takes_it_back (sibling with the granted folder's name as a prefix stays refused, ../ out of a grant refused, in_root ignores grants), rusti_own_folders_are_readable_but_not_writable, a_symlink_out_of_the_working_directory_is_judged_by_where_it_leads (unix: link to dir, to file, dangling; walk and substring grep do not follow), drive_and_unc_paths_outside_the_working_directory_are_refused (cfg(windows), not run here), add_dir_command_lists_adds_and_removes. walk_follows_links_only_when_asked moved under target/ because a link leading out of the project is now (correctly) not followed. cargo test: 138 unit + 11 rpc + 1 trust pass; rusti --self-test OK on Linux (cc, libc-dev and libssl-dev unpacked into a scratch dir, nothing installed system-wide). The Windows-only test was not run.
decisions: Only the file tools are fenced; shell commands are not sandboxed and the docs say so plainly. Decided with the captain's open question: restrict the file tools, leave shell coverage as the captain's call.
A refusal, not a prompt: the model cannot grant itself access, and the user's answer is /add-dir. A new permission prompt per outside read would be the old behaviour with extra clicks.
One /add-dir command with --remove instead of a second /remove-dir: fewer menu entries, and /re no longer matches a fourth command.

The guard's own hook point is not added: a pre_tool hook already sees every call's arguments and can refuse, which covers tightening the policy. Widening it from a hook is deliberately not possible (docs/extensions.md § hooks).
